primitives.name: Player-Confrontation Matrix
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Feature engineering:** unigrams/bigrams from commentary mapped to 19 batting features (response: attacked, beaten, defended, ...) × 12 bowling features (line/length: leg, slow, swing, moveAway, short, full, ...) → per-player *confrontation matrix* N (batting × bowling co-occurrence).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N_{ij}': 'count of co-occurrence between batting feature i and bowling feature j for a given player'}
primitives.assumptions: Commentary features accurately reflect delivery attributes and player responses; matrix entries are non-negative counts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player sample size < 150 deliveries, matrix becomes sparse and unreliable.

layer2.mapping: The confrontation matrix N encodes the statistical dependence structure between batting and bowling features, isomorphic to a contingency table used in correspondence analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized cell frequencies and marginal totals used in CA.

primitives.name: Correspondence Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Correspondence Analysis (CA):** SVD on the normalized, centered N → principal components F (batting) and G (bowling).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\tilde{N}': 'normalized and centered confrontation matrix', 'U, V': 'left/right singular vectors', '\\Sigma': 'singular values diagonal matrix'}
primitives.assumptions: Matrix N follows a chi-square distribution; row/column sums are fixed; SVD minimizes squared distances to reduced subspace.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N has zero variance across rows/columns, SVD fails to produce meaningful components.

layer2.mapping: CA maps the high-dimensional N into low-dimensional spaces F and G, enabling visualization and rule extraction through geometric relationships.
layer2.telemetry: Principal component scores F and G used in rule extraction and player clustering.

primitives.name: Rule Extraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Rule extraction:** for a batsman, strength rules from F_attacked: compute ⟨F_attacked, G_j⟩ for all bowling vectors; top-1/top-2 inner products = first/second strength rules.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{\\text{attacked}}': "batting feature vector for 'attacked' response", 'G_j': 'bowling feature vector for j-th bowling type', '\\langle \\cdot, \\cdot \\rangle': 'inner product between vectors'}
primitives.assumptions: Inner product captures similarity between batting and bowling feature vectors; rule validity depends on statistical significance of α ≠ 1.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F_attacked is orthogonal to all G_j, no strength rule can be extracted.

layer2.mapping: Rule extraction computes optimal bowling strategies for each batting style via vector alignment in the CA space.
layer2.telemetry: Top-k inner products define strength/weakness rules for individual players.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology begins with constructing a confrontation matrix N from unstructured cricket commentary, encoding co-occurrences of batting and bowling features. This matrix undergoes correspondence analysis (CA), which applies SVD to a normalized version of N, yielding principal components F (batting) and G (bowling). These components allow for the interpretation of player strengths and weaknesses through inner products. For example, a batsman’s strength against a particular bowling type is determined by maximizing the inner product between their batting feature vector (e.g., F_attacked) and the bowling feature vectors (G_j). The resulting rule set enables situational reasoning in GSE, while the rule vectors themselves are clustered using t-SNE to identify similar players. The method assumes that textual features capture meaningful delivery and response dynamics, and that statistical dependencies (α ≠ 1) in the matrix indicate actionable patterns. Failure modes include insufficient data leading to sparse matrices, or when features do not align with actual gameplay, causing misinterpretation of rules.
